title: Rational polyhedral cones have finite rational half-space descriptions
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q$-vector space [def-weil-field] [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], let $v_1,\ldots,v_m\in V$ (allowing $m=0$), and put $C=\{\sum_j q_jv_j:q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\}$. Then there are finitely many $\mathbf Q$-linear forms $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_s:V\to\mathbf Q$ (allowing $s=0$) such that $$C=\{x\in V:\lambda_i(x)\ge0\text{ for every }i\}.$$ This is the rational Minkowski--Weyl (finite H-cone) description; no pointedness or spanning hypothesis is required.

source.place: Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, rational polyhedral-cone description; Kato 1994, Toric singularities, is WANTED for a proof of the finite rational half-space form.
